evidence: Judge agent and model: task.toml [verifier.env] has REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "" (the shared block named in SKILL.md line 27); environment_mode = "separate". All five judge.toml files have only judge = "claude-code", mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template in [judge]; no model, reasoning_effort, temperature or weight; their headers up to [scoring] are identical to the frozen template. Pinned CLIs and browser: tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template and installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7, and Chromium through the Playwright CLI bundled with the pinned @playwright/mcp (so the browser revision follows that pin); every judge launches it with --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium. Shared tools: tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/tools/score.py and tests/.dockerignore are byte-identical (cmp) to the frozen template; test.sh runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1 and fixed suite budgets 1500 and 11100. Time rules: no criterion, note or instruction grades a calendar date, a displayed timestamp, an age, a relative date or any figure derived from the run date (searched all judge.toml files, app_context.md, instruction.md and environment/instructions for clock, date, timestamp, today, ago and similar). The only graded time rules are durations measured from an action inside the session (five-second run budget, about-five-second library refresh, graded with a ten-second allowance), so the result does not depend on the day of the run and no fixed clock is needed. The golden's new Date().toISOString() in server.js lines 71, 84, 111 feeds a stored timestamp that no criterion reads; crypto.randomUUID values in runtime.ts and app.tsx are internal nonces not graded. Evidence hashes: all 22 artifacts in raw-evidence-index.json match. Scripted golden results on these bytes report true for the timing criteria (cw_time_limit_recovery, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_newer_run_supersedes, cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget). RISKS that remain (not defects of this row, but not measured): (1) no configured judge run exists for these bytes, only a hosted run on an earlier candidate, so judge behaviour on the current wording is unmeasured; (2) cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (weight 2.0) and cw_newer_run_supersedes (weight 1.5) depend on the judge acting within a four-second wall-clock window after Run; each allows one void repeat and then tells the judge to fail the criterion ('fail this criterion and say that Stop could not be pressed in time'), so a slow judge turn could fail a conforming app twice by latency alone. This is a real-time sensitivity of the LLM judge, not a run-date dependency, and belongs to the criterion-reliability rows; the scripted golden does not measure judge latency. (3) Base images node:22-bookworm-slim and python:3.12-slim and the apt packages are tag-pinned, not digest-pinned; this is template-controlled and identical to the frozen template.
